pr.title: Validate CopyForDeref and DerefTemps better and remove them from runtime MIR
pr.description:

(split from my WIP rust-lang/rust#145344)

This PR:
- Removes `Rvalue::CopyForDeref` and `LocalInfo::DerefTemp` from runtime MIR
    - Using a new mir pass `EraseDerefTemps`
    - `CopyForDeref(x)` is turned into `Use(Copy(x))`
    - `DerefTemp` is turned into `Boring`
        - Not sure if this part is actually necessary, it made more sense in rust-lang/rust#145344 with `DerefTemp` storing actual data that I wanted to keep from having to be kept in sync with the rest of the body in runtime MIR
- Checks in validation that `CopyForDeref` and `DerefTemp` are only used together
- Removes special handling for `CopyForDeref` from many places
- Removes `CopyForDeref` from `custom_mir` reverting rust-lang/rust#111587
    - In runtime MIR simple copies can be used instead
    - In post cleanup analysis MIR it was already wrong to use due to the lack of support for creating `DerefTemp` locals
    - Possibly this should be its own PR?
 - Adds an argument to `deref_finder` to avoid creating new `DerefTemp`s and `CopyForDeref` in runtime MIR.
     - Ideally we would just avoid making intermediate derefs instead of fixing it at the end of a pass / during shim building
 - Removes some usages of `deref_finder` that I found out don't actually do anything

pr.author: beepster4096

analysis.originalLogic: Before this change, `Rvalue::CopyForDeref` and `LocalInfo::DerefTemp` were allowed as ordinary runtime-MIR constructs: codegen and many MIR passes special-cased `CopyForDeref` as a copy-like read, and validation only required that the `CopyForDeref` place type be dereferenceable. `Derefer`/`deref_finder` could also create these constructs in shims and coroutine bodies without distinguishing analysis MIR from runtime MIR. The old docs described `CopyForDeref` as a read whose only use is an immediately following deref with projections.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, runtime MIR could still contain `CopyForDeref(place)` and `DerefTemp` locals and treat them as normal runtime values: `CopyForDeref` was lowered as a plain copy by codegen/const-prop/GVN/etc., and a `DerefTemp` could be assigned by something other than `CopyForDeref` or accessed without first dereferencing it. That violates the intended alias invariant. The corrected design instead erases these constructs only after drop elaboration: `CopyForDeref(place)` becomes `Use(Copy(place))`, and the `DerefTemp` local becomes `Boring`, with validation forbidding both constructs in runtime MIR and enforcing their pairing before erasure.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies at the runtime phase (including shims and coroutine StateTransform output) that contain `DerefTemp` locals and/or `CopyForDeref` rvalues, where the copied place has a dereferenceable type. Analysis-phase MIR may contain them; runtime MIR must not.
analysis.summary: Runtime MIR must not contain `CopyForDeref` or `DerefTemp`. EraseDerefTemps rewrites `CopyForDeref(p)` to `Use(Copy(p))` and `DerefTemp` to `Boring` after AddRetag/ElaborateDrops, while Validator enforces that DerefTemps are dereferenceable, written only by CopyForDeref, and accessed only through a deref before erasure. deref_finder needs an explicit flag so runtime shims/coroutines do not recreate these analysis-only constructs.
analysis.trigger: A MIR construction or optimization path creates a `DerefTemp` local with `CopyForDeref`, or code reaches runtime lowering/codegen with either construct still present; alternatively a `DerefTemp` is assigned a non-`CopyForDeref` rvalue or read directly instead of through a deref.
preconditions: A `DerefTemp` local must have a dereferenceable type.
A `DerefTemp` may only be written by `CopyForDeref`; otherwise it may only be accessed through a deref (its first place projection is indirect).
`EraseDerefTemps` must run after `AddRetag`/`ElaborateDrops` but before `ElaborateBoxDerefs` and codegen.
Runtime-MIR `deref_finder` callers (shims and coroutine StateTransform) must pass `add_deref_metadata = false` so they emit plain copies and `Boring` locals.
pitfalls: Do not erase `CopyForDeref` before drop elaboration: it is not equivalent to a normal copy for drop elaboration.
Do not assume `CopyForDeref(p)` and `Use(Copy(p))` are interchangeable in every MIR phase; the rewrite is only valid at the runtime erasure boundary.
Do not treat a `DerefTemp` as `Boring` while an analysis pass still relies on the transparent-alias metadata.
Do not allow `DerefTemp` locals to be read directly or assigned by non-`CopyForDeref` rvalues.
Checking only that the `CopyForDeref` place is dereferenceable is insufficient; the local-info pairing must also be validated.
analysis.testStrategy: Use mir-opt MIR dumps around the erasure boundary: construct cases where `Derefer`/`deref_finder` creates a deref temp, then check that the `EraseDerefTemps`/runtime dump contains `_N = copy (...)` rather than `_N = deref_copy (...)` and no remaining `CopyForDeref`/`DerefTemp`. The supplied coroutine StateTransform and shim expectations show this exact replacement of `deref_copy` by `copy`. For validation, add negative compiler tests that violate each invariant (CopyForDeref/DerefTemp present in runtime MIR, assignment to DerefTemp not using CopyForDeref, direct read of DerefTemp, non-dereferenceable DerefTemp), noting that the `custom_mir` `mir_copy_for_deref` helper was removed, so constructing such malformed runtime MIR may require internal test infrastructure rather than the public custom-MIR dialect.
evidence: //! This pass converts all `DerefTemp` locals into normal temporaries
//! and turns their `CopyForDeref` rvalues into normal copies.
It may only be written to by a `CopyForDeref` and otherwise only accessed through a deref.
In runtime MIR, it is replaced with a normal `Boring` local.
`CopyForDeref` should have been removed in runtime MIR
`DerefTemp` should have been removed in runtime MIR
`DerefTemp` locals must only be dereferenced or directly assigned to
`DerefTemp` should only be used for dereferenceable types
